evals.prompt: We're Casa del Pueblo, a 501(c)(3) community center in Las Cruces, NM serving mostly Latino families (about 3,000 visitors a month). For the November 2027 city election we want to (1) host a forum for the 4 mayoral candidates, (2) run a voter registration drive, and (3) send GOTV reminders. Help us plan all three so we stay compliant.
evals.expected_output: Plans each activity against the absolute 501(c)(3) candidate-intervention ban using the nonpartisanship factors, with forum, registration and GOTV designs, documentation, disclaimers, training and pre-clearance.
assertions: States that 501(c)(3)s are absolutely prohibited from intervening for or against any candidate, with no dollar threshold, distinguishing this from 501(h) lobbying limits
Forum plan invites all legally qualified candidates in writing with equal notice, uses an identical neutral question set, a neutral moderator, and neutral handling of an empty seat

Registration drive targets unregistered visitors generally by nonpartisan criteria, uses the nonpartisan national or state form, a scripted neutral volunteer pitch, and does not track party affiliation
GOTV reminders are factual (deadlines, early voting, polling lookup) and sent at volumes consistent with normal communications
Recommends documenting even-handedness per activity (invitations, materials) plus a 'does not endorse any candidate' disclaimer and pre-cycle staff/volunteer training
Recommends pre-clearance by a designated reviewer or counsel given exempt-status risk

evals.prompt: Can our ED post on her personal Instagram that she's voting for Jensen for county commissioner? She's kinda well known as our ED.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a staff member's personal endorsement is allowed on personal time and accounts but must never use organizational resources or identity, recommends safeguards and training, and suggests counsel review for a high-profile ED.
assertions: Explains that personal political activity is permitted on the ED's own time and personal account but must not use org letterhead, logo, email signature, official accounts, or resources
Advises against the post being framed in her organizational capacity (e.g., speaking as the ED or tagging the org)
Recommends pre-cycle staff training on the personal vs. organizational distinction
Recommends checking with counsel given the absolute ban and her high public profile

evals.prompt: Our board wants to (a) publish a scorecard grading the state legislative candidates A–F on housing votes, and (b) campaign hard for Measure 4, the affordable housing bond on the same ballot. A board member says we can't do either because we're a 501(c)(3). Who's right?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the absolute bar on candidate intervention (the graded scorecard is high-risk de facto endorsement) from ballot-measure advocacy, which a c3 may do subject to lobbying limits, and recommends counsel review.
assertions: Identifies the A–F candidate scorecard as a high-risk de facto endorsement/opposition and advises against it, offering a neutral side-by-side guide using candidates' own words instead
Explains that a 501(c)(3) may support or oppose a ballot measure because it is issue advocacy, not candidate intervention
Notes ballot-measure advocacy counts toward 501(h) lobbying limits if applicable and should be tracked (coordinating with legislative advocacy)
States the board member is partly wrong — candidates are an absolute bar, ballot measures are capped, not banned
Recommends counsel review or pre-clearance before publishing

should_not_trigger.query: Our 501(c)(3) wants to endorse a city council candidate who champions our issues — how do we set up a 501(c)(4) to do that legally?
Write an action alert urging supporters to email their state reps to vote yes on the housing bond bill in committee next week.
